summary: Surveyed all 310 listed Lean files under Complexitylib/Circuits (445 to 147843 bytes; all in the main source tree, no scripts, tests, generated, or vendored files). A line-start declaration grep (theorem|lemma|def|structure|class|instance|inductive|abbrev|example|axiom|opaque, with modifiers and attributes) found declarations in 305 files. The 5 zero-declaration files were read completely: each holds only a module header, public imports, and a module docstring, so they are pure import aggregators that FILTER-007 keeps primary-eligible (ranked lower, not excluded). All files are retained.

summary: Inspected all 36 Lean files in the Complexitylib/Circuits/Shallow and Complexitylib/Circuits/SparseSynthesis directories. Every file contains substantial formal mathematical content: definitions (def, abbrev, noncomputable def), theorem/lemma statements with proofs, and mathematical constructions related to shallow circuit upper bounds for symmetric functions (Lecomte-Ramakrishnan) and sparse synthesis/square-root continuity of circuit complexity (Chashkin-style). No file is a pure import aggregator — each contains executable/formal declarations beyond imports, module docs, and whitespace. Per FILTER-007, pure import aggregators would be navigation data, but none exist in this set. Per FILTER-004 and FILTER-021, hard exclusion requires prover-aware verification of no formal math content, which is not the case here. All files are retained as primary-eligible.

summary: Inspected all 19 Lean files in the Complexitylib/Circuits/KarchmerWigderson directory. Every file contains substantial formal mathematical content: core definitions (inductive types, structures), theorem statements with proofs, and mathematical constructions related to Karchmer-Wigderson protocols, top-down communication lower bounds (Korten's adversary), and wire lower bounds for parity and majority. The aggregation files (Circuit.lean, Rounds.lean, TopDown.lean, Majority.lean) each declare public theorems beyond imports, so none qualify as pure import aggregators per FILTER-007. Per FILTER-004 and FILTER-021, no file meets the high evidence bar for hard exclusion — all hold unique searchable formal mathematics.
